bestBets.overview: WANT A WINNER raced a bit flat first up. He should improve significantly off that run and William Pike retains the ride. THE CALABRESE has been racing well all preparation. raceTips.comment: Capper Thirtynine brings real intrigue on WA debut for Aaron Mitchell with some really strong eastern states form from his recent runs. Figures stack up, think he’ll run well on WA debut as a pretty versatile horse who hasn’t spent much time off so he should carry some real residual. The Calabrese has been holding his form all campaign and thought he was enormous from his settling position in defeat last start, small field really suits his racing pattern. Want A Winner can definitely bounce back but he’s very short at $2.40? Bit of Pike tax I feel and while he could just about lead this with the lack of tempo in this on paper and he raced fierce in running first up, can’t hide the fact he was very disappointing. Ice Pick Nick has been forgotten by the market, solid trial and high quality galloper on his day.

If he gets clear room and repeats that effort he can give it a big shake again. BONNIE LAD beat a similar line-up last start and has claims again. AMAROO STAR was flying last preparation and attacks this off an attractive trial win.

raceTips.comment: Amaroo Star resumes and loved the sharpness of the trial leading in, in what was a pretty hot little heat. Just looks mapped to get the gun run right on the hammer of a hot tempo with the speed engaged here and was a first up winner last campaign with a near identical run in transit to what I expect he’ll enjoy here. Somewhat surprised he’s each way? Could be a big day for Simon Miller. Swingman is a tough, on speed sprinter who bumped into some very sharp ones for much of last campaign. Trialled without the shades and still may not yet have reached his ceiling? Long Service Leaf was unlucky but how unlucky last weekend? Bit torn on the run and barrier 1 leaves him needing luck in running once again. Excess Baggage has a ripping turn of foot but does leave herself with a bit of work to do and this race is comfortably stronger than the one she contested first up.

raceTips.comment: Traditionally tricky little Westspeed. Champagne Crusader was a solid effort first up behind In Confidence (who should take care of them in race 2) and second up last campaign ran a monster race in the 3YO Magic Millions Trophy behind Twisted Steel. Maps for a great run from the low draw and should only come on, each-way seems very backable. Roaming America is an exciting horse for Mack Hall and his team who can win this fresh (trying not to read too much into a visually unappealing trial leading in). He’s on the up and ran 3rd to Ladies Pro beaten under 2L the last time we saw him at the races, also very versatile. True Fiction hasn’t run a bad race all campaign and runs for the Pontiff. Slick has a lot of upside, trial was good leading in too, just drawn very awkwardly and likely has to get right back as a result.

YES I KNOW was well supported in the betting in his local debut but he settled at the tail and failed to fire a shot. No surprise to see him improve sharply. RIPPER FAROOQ next best.

raceTips.comment: Sherpa Express looks a very talented, lightly raced sprinter who steps out for the first time this campaign off a nice trial behind the sharp Amaroo Star leading in. Last prep had two starts, 2nd behind Luana Miss first up in a Placid Ark savaging the line and 3rd in a Lee Steere (both at black type level) behind classy filly Hot And High. 58.5kgs after the claim, drawn soft, not an overly strong Grad, should really be making his presence felt here with the run he’s likely to enjoy. Yes I Know had everything that could go wrong, go wrong on WA debut after a huge wave of betting support. Eastern states forms and figures well and truly stack up, happy to give him a mulligan. Ripper Farooq was a really strong winner in good time first up this campaign over the 1000m, looks to have come back in great order but likely has to do some work here from the gate. God’s Gate has been an enigma across his career but the best version of him showed up last start at Pinjarra.

bestBets.overview: SENSESSIONAL attacks this first up off a strong trial. He has a terrific record at the track and draws to get every chance in running. CAPTAIN PLUTO flies fresh and Pike rides. He should be motoring late. SILVER EYE has plenty of ability and looked very sharp in a recent trial effort. ANGEL UNDERCOVER ran well first up and Chris Parnham goes on for an apprentice.

raceTips.comment: Think Silver Eye looks a great each-way bet in the feature. Came of age last campaign as a horse who was formally regarded as a 1000m sprinter where he won 3 races stretching from the 1000m up to 1500m and placed in both Bunbury and Pinjarra Cups. Many of these are first up and of those that trialled leading in, his was comfortably the most impressive piece of work. If Nottle can find the three deep line with him and have him blending in on straightening, I think he’s a great winning chance at a genuine each-way price. Angel Undercover having the run under the belt (and a very good one at that) is going to hold her in very good stead with Chris Parnham jumping on, quality mare on her day with a ripping finish on her. Sensessional trialled well for his return, draws soft and love the 1400m kick-off point for him. Captain Pluto was a bit of a fresh sensation when he arrived here in WA and while the Pike booking will get some on that fact alone, he’ll be last with 60kgs off the back of a pair of trials that can only be considered as iffy leading in.

raceTips.comment: Average race to finish. Berry Blast probably has the most upside of this lot and while she didn't beat much last start she did so as impressively as she could have, she's tractable, she's got a turn of foot and she maps super here. Statewide brings the A1 formlines but gee he gets a long way back and will do so again here from the draw, if Steve Parnham can have him on them at the corner he'll probably go past but doesn't appear the easiest horse to ride? Belle Journee gets Pike and has caught the eye late in both previous runs since her first up win at Bunbury. Vexatious Rose has turned a corner.
